openai.source: Orca codex-model-pricing.ts:13-81, the only witness for these rows: they are OpenAI's models, so the vendor reference this tree can check against does not cover them. A wrong row here produces a plausible dollar figure no test can catch. `long_context_threshold_tokens` is LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD_TOKENS (codex-model-pricing.ts:11) and is a property of ONE request, which is why the surcharge is applied per turn. `reasoning_tiers` are the effort words an id may wear (REASONING_TIER_SUFFIXES, :83); they say nothing about its price. Matching: an id is normalised (tier stripped), then the row whose `ids` entry equals it or is a `-`-segment prefix of it answers, longest first; `exact` names an alias a row prices only when spelled exactly, never as a prefix — the bare gpt-5.6 routes to Sol, and a gpt-5.6- prefix would swallow terra, luna and any cheaper variant the vendor ships next.

anthropic.source: Cross-checked twice: Orca claude-model-pricing.ts:22-50 and the claude-api reference's current-models table agree on every row. Only `input` and `output` are listed per row; the cache rates are DEFINED as multiples of input (claude-api skill, shared/prompt-caching.md:141: reads ~0.1x, five-minute writes 1.25x, hour-long writes 2x) and are written once here instead of per row, where two more numbers per row would be two more places to drift. Orca carries a single cacheWrite and prices every cache-creation token at the five-minute rate, 37.5% under on hour-long writes, which are 70% of this machine's corpus. Matching: an id is lowercased, an anthropic/ or anthropic: prefix dropped and dots turned to dashes; the row whose family key (its id without claude-) the id names, followed by a non-digit, answers, longest first; a `legacy_base` row answers only for its strict shapes (bare, -thinking, -20YYMMDD, @20YYMMDD); and `prices_unknown_members_of` names the family whose point releases nobody has taught this table about bill at that row — the current rate, because three times too much (the legacy Opus 4 rate) is a worse answer than a little too little.

rows.note: Reads a cached prefix at $0.25 per million, a fortieth of input and a quarter of Fable 5's rate (claude-api skill, shared/model-migration.md, Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 -> Pricing).

The ORIGINAL Opus 4 bills at three times the modern Opus rate (claude-model-pricing.ts:31-32); an old id normalised onto the modern row would under-report by two thirds, and a future point release matched here would be over-charged three times, so the shape is strict.
The one row with a date on it: $2/$10 through 2026-08-31 is the vendor's own launch price, billed on the day a message was sent. After the window closes the row stops applying by itself.

typesafe.source: TypeSafe's launch post for its System One models (https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev, 2026-09-15), re-read 2026-09-17 for docs/design/jev-decision-shadow-20260917.md: input $0.042 per million tokens, output free. A System One call writes no prose and bills input only, and the post names no cache rates, so none are written here. `announced` sits beside the price because an early-access price is the kind that moves. Matching: the exact id, case-insensitive — a dated or pinned id no row names is unpriced, never billed at a neighbour's rate.
